main_text.p: Parata sunt tibi regna coelorum: potes imitari maiestatem Dei ut absq; peccato sis. Accepisti enim liberi arbitrii potestatem, & legis scientiam, per quam consequaris quod volueris. decipiuntq; blanditiis miseros, & maxime mulierculas oneratas peccatis, quę circumferuntur omni vento doctrinæ, &c. Ibid.
Nobis agentibus patienter, & exspectantibus miserorum salutem, præueniunt hæretici, & nos suo appellant nomine, cæci ducētes cæcos in foueam. In 29. caput.

Sicut quondam Pseudoprophetæ falsis vaticiniis & mendacibus promissis gentem Iudæorum seducebant: ita & nunc hæretici atq; schismatici fictis opinionibus & dolosis argumentarionibus corda simplicium à veritate rectæ fidei & statu bonorum operum subuertere certant. lib.1. Commentar.in 2.caput Lamentatio-num.

Despiciunt Sion, & confidunt sibi in monte Samariæ, in superbia videlicet dogmatum peruersorum, quæ putant esse sublimia, & per has prædicationes fraudulentas vindemiant atque populantur principia gentiū, ut miraculo doctrinarum potentes quosq; gentilium ad errorem hæreticum pertrahant. In 16. caput Ezechielis.

page.notes: Printed text is in the 16th–17th century Latin style; the faint mirrored (show-through) text from the other side of the leaf was left out. "Ibid." and the bracketed-style references are italic in the print. "Commentar" is set with a decorative initial that I could not read with certainty and is copied as "Commentar" [?]. The argumentarionibus spelling is as printed. Hyphens at line ends are kept where the print hyphenates (va-ticiniis, Lamentatio-num, nu-).
